++# 📋 Relatório de Auditoria Técnica — brazil-wildfire-risk-forecast
++
++**Auditor:** Cientista de Dados Sênior & Revisor Técnico de Machine Learning  
++**Data:** 20 de Outubro de 2026  
++**Status da Auditoria:** FASE 1 CONCLUÍDA — Aguardando Aprovação para Fase 2  
++
++---
++
++## 1. Resumo Honesto do Estado Atual
++
++O projeto apresenta maturidade muito superior à média de portfólios de nível júnior: é um pipeline ponta a ponta funcional, construído com 10 anos de dados reais oficiais (290 mil focos do INPE e reanálise MERRA-2 da NASA), cobrindo mais de 1,8 milhão de registros espaço-temporais. Possui validação temporal real (treino $\le 2023$, teste $2024-2025$), baselines comparativos implementados, explicabilidade via SHAP, API REST documentada e dashboard interativo funcional.
++
++Contudo, sob o escrutínio de um revisor técnico exigente, foram identificadas **fragilidades metodológicas e de engenharia** que comprometeriam a credibilidade do candidato em uma entrevista técnica profunda:
++1. **Distorção de Calibração Probabilística**: A calibração isotônica pós-treino colapsou a ordenação do modelo (PR-AUC caiu de 0,6277 para 0,3468), forçando o deploy do modelo com probabilidades não calibradas devido ao `scale_pos_weight`.
++2. **Dependência Excessiva de Coordenadas Estáticas**: As features `lat_center` e `lon_center` dominam o SHAP com peso 2,5 vezes superior ao das variáveis climáticas, evidenciando memorização espacial em vez de aprendizado de causalidade biofísica.
++3. **Validação Espacial por Células Aleatórias**: O `GroupKFold` agrupa observações por célula individual, mas distribui células vizinhas aleatoriamente entre treino e validação, permitindo vazamento indireto por autocorrelação espacial através da feature `neighbor_fire_7d`.
++4. **Tratamento de Borda no Alvo**: A função de criação do alvo mascara os últimos 7 dias da série histórica como classe 0 (`NaN > 0 \rightarrow False`), mascarando a incerteza na fronteira temporal.
++5. **Gaps de Engenharia e MLOps**: Ausência de esteira de CI/CD (GitHub Actions), scripts de download sem testes unitários com mock, API sem validação de bounding box geográfico (aceita coordenadas fora do Mato Grosso e extrapola), e dependência de `make` que falha nativamente no Windows.
++
++---
++
++## 2. Teste de Reprodutibilidade
++
++Foi realizado o teste de execução do fluxo completo seguindo estritamente as instruções documentadas:
++
++| Comando / Etapa | Status | Diagnóstico Técnico |
++|---|:---:|---|
++| `git clone` e `python -m venv` | **Aprovado** | Ambiente criado sem conflitos no Python 3.12. |
++| `pip install -r requirements.txt` | **Aprovado** | Todas as 28 dependências principais e secundárias instalaram com sucesso com versões fixadas. |
++| `pytest tests/ -v` | **Aprovado** | 13 de 13 testes passaram em 2.42 segundos (incluindo teste anti-vazamento e API). |
++| `uvicorn api.main:app` | **Aprovado** | API inicializa perfeitamente; endpoint `POST /predict` responde com latência média de 24 ms. |
++| `streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py` | **Aprovado com Ressalva** | Dashboard abre e mapa Folium renderiza. **Ressalva**: Folium emite `UserWarning: CartoDB tiles now require an API key`. |
++| `make all` / `make test` | **Falha no Windows** | O utilitário `make` não é instalado por padrão no Windows PowerShell (`The term 'make' is not recognized`). Além disso, o comando `clean` usa sintaxe Unix (`rm -rf`) incompatível com o PowerShell nativo. |
++| Download Completo (`download_climate.py`) | **Aprovado com Ressalva** | Baixa 506 células com sucesso, mas realiza 506 chamadas HTTP sequenciais/paralelas demorando ~9 minutos. Depende 100% da estabilidade da API pública da NASA no momento da execução. |
++| `docker build` | **Não Verificado** | O Docker Desktop não está instalado no host Windows deste ambiente de desenvolvimento. O Dockerfile é sintaticamente válido, mas a execução do container não pôde ser comprovada em runtime. |
++
++---
++
++## 3. Revisão Metodológica
++
++### 3.1 Vazamento de Dados (Data Leakage)
++- **Variáveis Retrospectivas**: **Aprovado sem vazamento futuro**. Todas as janelas móveis de contagem de focos (`fire_count_7d`, `14d`, `30d`), médias climáticas e precipitação acumulada utilizam estritamente dados até o dia $D$ da previsão. O teste unitário `test_no_future_leak_in_fire_features` valida programaticamente que injeções futuras não contaminam as features passadas.
++- **Normalização e Escalonamento**: **Aprovado sem vazamento**. O `StandardScaler` da Regressão Logística é ajustado estritamente em `X_train` (`fit_transform`) e aplicado no teste (`transform`).
++- **Latência Operacional de Reanálise (Vazamento Operacional)**: **Alerta Metodológico**. O modelo utiliza a temperatura máxima (`T2M_MAX`) e precipitação (`PRECTOTCORR`) consolidadas do dia $D$ para prever $[D+1, D+7]$. Na operação real, a reanálise MERRA-2 da NASA possui latência de disponibilização de 2 a 3 dias. Em produção estrita, o pipeline necessitaria ou de previsão numérica de tempo (GFS/ECMWF) ou de defasagem de 2 dias nas features climáticas.
++- **Tratamento de Borda Temporal do Alvo**: **Falha Leve**. Na função `_compute_target`, o cálculo `.shift(-1).rolling(7).sum().shift(-6)` gera valores `NaN` para os últimos 7 dias de 2025. A comparação `future_fires > 0` transforma silenciosamente esses `NaN` em `False` (`0`), e a linha `dataset.dropna(subset=['target'])` não descarta nenhuma linha. O modelo é treinado acreditando que os últimos 7 dias de 2025 não tiveram fogo por observação, e não por falta de horizonte futuro.
++
++### 3.2 Estratégia de Validação Espaçotemporal
++- **Validação Temporal**: **Excelente**. Treinamento estritamente em dados históricos (2016–2023, 1,48 milhão de amostras) e teste cego em anos futuros (2024–2025, 370 mil amostras), testando a resiliência do modelo à seca extrema de 2024.
++- **Validação Espacial**: **Parcialmente Eficaz**. O Optuna utiliza `GroupKFold(n_splits=3, groups=train_df["grid_id"])`. Embora impeça que a mesma célula esteja no treino e no teste do fold, as 506 células são sorteadas aleatoriamente pela grade. Células adjacentes ficam em folds distintos, permitindo vazamento indireto via dependência espacial e através da feature `neighbor_fire_7d`. O padrão-ouro exige **blocos espaciais contíguos** (ex.: quadrantes Norte, Centro e Sul) ou **buffer geográfico (Dead Zones)**.
++- **Validação Walk-Forward**: Ausente. Foi realizada apenas uma divisão temporal fixa, sem avaliar janelas expansivas multi-ano (ex.: treina 2016-2020 $\rightarrow$ testa 2021; treina 2016-2021 $\rightarrow$ testa 2022).
++
++### 3.3 Definição do Alvo e Unidade Espaçotemporal
++- **Clareza e Coerência**: **Excelente**. Grade regular de 0,5° (~56 km) alinhada à resolução do modelo atmosférico MERRA-2. Janela de 7 dias à frente compatível com mobilização logística de brigadas. Alvo binário ($\ge 1$ foco) imune a ruídos finos de contagem térmica de múltiplos sensores.
++
++### 3.4 Desbalanceamento e Métricas
++- **Distribuição**: ~19% positivos no treino e ~16% no teste.
++- **Seleção de Métricas**: **Excelente**. Adoção correta do PR-AUC (Precision-Recall AUC) como métrica primária em vez de acurácia ou ROC-AUC isolada. Avaliação complementar por ROC-AUC, Brier score e Recall@P50.
++- **Ponderação de Classe**: Adoção de `scale_pos_weight = 4.12` no LightGBM melhorou expressivamente o Recall (66,85% com precisão $\ge 50\%$), mas inflou as probabilidades brutas preditas, penalizando o Brier score (0,1468 vs 0,1072 da climatologia).
++
++### 3.5 Baselines
++- **Persistência e Climatologia**: Implementados e superados pelo LightGBM em PR-AUC e ROC-AUC.
++- **Ressalva Metodológica na Persistência**: A probabilidade de persistência foi modelada pela fórmula ad-hoc $1 - \exp(-\text{raw} / 3.0)$. A constante $3.0$ é arbitrária. O rigor acadêmico exige ou o indicador binário puro ou o cálculo da frequência empírica condicional no conjunto de treino.
++- **Climatologia como Benchmark Real**: A climatologia pura atingiu ROC-AUC respeitável de 0,8525 e melhor Brier score (0,1072) do que o LightGBM, provando a força da sazonalidade cíclica do cerrado brasileiro. O LightGBM demonstrou seu valor ao superar a climatologia em mais de 11 pontos de PR-AUC (0,6277 vs 0,5159), capturando as anomalias climáticas dinâmicas de seca.
++
++### 3.6 Calibração e Análise de Erros
++- **Falha na Calibração**: O `CalibratedClassifierCV` com regressão isotônica colapsou a ordenação do modelo (PR-AUC caiu de 0,6277 para 0,3468). Isso ocorreu porque a calibração isotônica pós-treino sobre probabilidades já distorcidas pelo `scale_pos_weight` esmagou as previsões em torno da frequência base. O modelo em produção atua sem calibração probabilística formal.
++- **Análise de Erros**: Conduzida por mês, evidenciando alta acurácia na estação chuvosa (>81%) e queda para 67% nos meses de transição (outubro). Falta análise de erro desagregada por macrorregião (biomas: Amazônia vs Cerrado vs Pantanal) e por anomalia anual.
++
++### 3.7 Explicabilidade (SHAP)
++- **Comportamento Físico**: As variáveis climáticas comportam-se de acordo com a física do fogo (chuva inibe risco, umidade baixa eleva risco, noites quentes aumentam risco, focos recentes impulsionam contágio).
++- **Risco de Overfitting Espacial**: `lat_center` (|SHAP| = 2.42) e `lon_center` (|SHAP| = 1.08) dominam com folga as variáveis meteorológicas. O modelo está se apoiando excessivamente em "onde está no mapa" em detrimento de "qual é o estado biofísico da vegetação". Sem variáveis de cobertura do solo (MapBiomas) ou biomassa (NDVI), as coordenadas atuam como atalho estatístico.
++

++## 8. Pontos Fortes para Defender em Entrevista
++
++1. **Volume e Autenticidade dos Dados**: O candidato trabalhou com **1,85 milhão de linhas reais** e 290 mil eventos de fogo ao longo de 10 anos, lidando com os desafios reais de escalabilidade de memória, formatos colunares (Parquet) e tipos compactos (`float32`).
++2. **Defesa Consciente do Satélite de Referência**: Saber explicar com clareza por que escolheu o sensor MODIS vespertino (`AQUA_M-T`) em vez de inflar os dados misturando múltiplos satélites demonstra maturidade incomum em séries temporais ambientais.
++3. **Validação Temporal Estrita (Out-of-Time)**: O modelo foi treinado até 2023 e testado cegamente nos anos de 2024 e 2025, provando capacidade de generalização diante do ano mais atípico de queimadas da história recente do Pantanal e Cerrado.
++4. **Superação Comprovada de Baselines Relevantes**: Demonstrar empiricamente que o LightGBM superou uma climatologia histórica refinada em mais de 11 pontos de PR-AUC prova que a complexidade do algoritmo se justifica na prática.
++5. **Cultura de Testes com Detecção Ativa de Data Leakage**: Ter um teste automatizado no Pytest (`test_no_future_leak_in_fire_features`) que valida matematicamente a contenção temporal é um diferencial técnico de alto impacto para uma vaga júnior/pleno.
++6. **Entrega de Produto Funcional**: Disponibilizar API com latência de 24 ms e aplicação Streamlit que opera tanto com banco de dados completo quanto em modo demo leve demonstra visão de engenharia orientada a produto.

++# Baseline Technical & Scientific Audit Report
++**Project:** Brazil Wildfire Risk Forecast (`brazil-wildfire-risk-forecast`)  
++**Commit Hash Audited:** `1b47873d84894a052712bbdcc5d2616be927cc10`  
++**Date:** October 2026  
++**Auditing Committee:** Senior ML/MLOps Engineer, Spatiotemporal Data Scientist, Remote Sensing Researcher, Python/FastAPI/Streamlit Software Engineer, Independent Scientific Reproducibility Auditor.
++
++---
++
++## 1. Executive Summary
++
++This report establishes the baseline technical and scientific audit of the `brazil-wildfire-risk-forecast` repository. The project has substantial foundations: 10 years of INPE satellite data and NASA POWER climate reanalysis, structured modular Python packages, multi-horizon targets, automated tests, DVC DAG, MLflow tracking, and Docker/Streamlit serving.
++
++However, an exhaustive line-by-line inspection and runtime audit across the entire codebase revealed critical methodological, architectural, and data integrity flaws:
++1. **Model Serialization Incompatibility (CI Crash):** Model artifacts were serialized with `scikit-learn 1.9.1` (where `multi_class` was removed), but `requirements.txt` pins `scikit-learn==1.5.2`. Loading these models under scikit-learn 1.5.2 triggers `AttributeError: 'LogisticRegression' object has no attribute 'multi_class'`, breaking GitHub Actions CI.
++2. **Synthetic Mock Inference in API (`_build_features`):** The API does not compute or lookup current observations; instead, it matches an arbitrary historical row with a similar day-of-year (e.g., from 2017) to predict any requested date (even 2026), overwriting query coordinates with row data.
++3. **Temporal Label Leakage Across Boundaries:** For a 7-day forward horizon, training labels for December 25–31, 2023 incorporate fire events from January 1–7, 2024 (the out-of-time test set). No temporal purging or embargo was enforced.
++4. **In-Sample Probability Calibration:** The LightGBM model was trained on 2016–2023, and then its in-sample predictions on 2023 were used to fit the Platt scaling calibrator. The calibrator was fitted on overconfident training predictions, not an independent holdout.
++5. **Missing Geographic Masking (154 Cells Outside Mato Grosso):** The grid was created as a bounding box without territorial polygon clipping. Over 30% of the grid (154 of 506 cells) lies outside Mato Grosso and received 0 fires for 10 years straight because INPE data was state-filtered, artificially inflating negative observations by >560,000 samples.
++6. **Data Imputation Distortions:** `nan_to_num(nan=0.0)` replaces missing temperatures with 0.0°C (an extreme freeze in tropical Mato Grosso), and missing precipitation is imputed as rainless, corrupting the physical features.
++7. **Silent Tracking Failures in MLflow:** A key mismatch (`r['Model']` vs `r['model']`) threw a `KeyError` that was silently swallowed, preventing experiment logging during `train.py`.
++8. **Unfair Recurrent Benchmark Evaluation:** The PyTorch LSTM was evaluated on a 4-day downsampled subset (91,080 samples) rather than the full test set (366,344 samples) used for LightGBM.
++
++All original baseline artifacts and reports have been permanently preserved in `reports/baseline_v1/` for transparent before-and-after comparison.
++
++---
++

++## 3. Detailed Audit by Component
++
++### 3.1 P0: GitHub Actions and Model Serialization
++- **Affected File:** `models/platt_calibrator.joblib`, `models/platt_calibrator_1d.joblib`, `models/platt_calibrator_3d.joblib`, `requirements.txt:5`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:29`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  ```python
++  # In scikit-learn 1.9.1, LogisticRegression removed the `multi_class` attribute.
++  # When pickled in 1.9.1, the joblib dictionary does not contain 'multi_class'.
++  # In scikit-learn 1.5.2 (pinned in requirements.txt), predict_proba() executes:
++  # if self.multi_class == "ovr": ... -> AttributeError!
++  ```
++- **Evidence:** Confirmed via Python inspection:
++  `hasattr(joblib.load('models/platt_calibrator.joblib'), 'multi_class') == False`.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Implement a standalone, version-agnostic Platt scaling class (`PlattCalibrator`) storing raw coefficients $(\alpha, \beta)$ and computing the logistic sigmoid natively via `scipy.special.expit` or NumPy without relying on sklearn internal attributes.
++  2. Regenerate all serialized artifacts under a controlled environment.
++  3. Record artifact metadata in `training_metadata.json` (`sklearn_version`, `python_version`, `numpy_version`, `timestamp`, `sha256`).
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** `pytest tests/ -v` and API `/predict` and `/explain` endpoints must execute cleanly across Python 3.11 and 3.12 without attribute errors.
++
++### 3.2 P0: API Feature Construction (`_build_features`)
++- **Affected File:** `api/main.py:152-203`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  Lines 189–197 match any input date to an arbitrary past record with the closest day of the year:
++  ```python
++  target_doy = day_of_year
++  cell_doy = cell_data["date"].dt.dayofyear
++  closest_idx = (cell_doy - target_doy).abs().idxmin()
++  row = cell_data.loc[closest_idx]
++  for col in _feature_cols:
++      if col in row.index and pd.notna(row[col]):
++          features[col] = float(row[col])  # Overwrites query lat_center/lon_center!
++  ```
++  This returns mock predictions based on random historical years. Furthermore, line 201 has a duplicated return statement, and lines 284–285 silently fall back to the 7-day model if a 1-day or 3-day model is missing.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Replace this logic with an explicit temporal inference contract supporting:
++     - `historical_replay`: Retrospective inference requiring exact data from `issue_date`.
++     - `operational_forecast`: Real-time operational mode. If live stream data is absent, return HTTP 503 Service Unavailable with an informative message.
++  2. Implement an explicit contract schema: `issue_date`, `observation_cutoff`, `target_start`, `target_end`, `data_timestamp`, `data_source`, `model_version`, `inference_mode`.
++  3. Never overwrite query spatial coordinates with cell centroid values unless documented.
++  4. Remove silent horizon fallbacks: if horizon 1d or 3d is requested and unavailable, raise HTTP 503.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Querying a specific date returns features from that exact date, and querying unsupported dates returns a clear error code instead of fictitious data.
++
++### 3.3 P0: Temporal Leakage & Embargo
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train.py:289-294`, `src/data/process_data.py:124-126`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  For forward horizon $H=7$, targets on day $D$ look forward to $[D+1, D+7]$. Training with `date.dt.year <= 2023` means rows from December 25 to December 31, 2023, have target labels constructed using fire counts from January 1 to January 7, 2024 (the test set).
++- **Evidence:** `train_df["date"].max()` is `2023-12-31`. For that row, `target_7d` is computed over `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-07`.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Implement strict temporal purging: training samples must end at `test_start_date - H days` (e.g. December 24, 2023 for 7d; December 28 for 3d; December 30 for 1d).
++  2. Enforce the same purge across all folds in walk-forward expanding window validation (e.g. 2020 vs 2021).
++  3. Add automated tests that assert `max(train_df['date']) + pd.Timedelta(days=H) < min(test_df['date'])`.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Zero label overlap across temporal boundaries, verified by automated unit tests.
++
++### 3.4 P0: In-Sample Calibration
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train.py:413-435`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  `final_model.fit(X_train, y_train)` fits on all of 2016–2023. Then lines 426–434 predict on `val_cal_mask = train_df["date"].dt.year == 2023` using `final_model`. Because the tree model already memorized 2023, the calibrator is trained on in-sample, overconfident probabilities.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Implement true out-of-sample calibration:
++     - Approach A (Out-of-Fold): Generate out-of-fold predictions across training folds or walk-forward windows.
++     - Approach B (Strict Temporal Holdout): Train the base model on 2016–2022; calibrate strictly on independent 2023 out-of-sample predictions.
++  2. Compare Platt Scaling and Isotonic Regression against uncalibrated probabilities.
++  3. Compute Brier score, Log Loss, and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on the untouched 2024–2025 test set.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Calibrator is fitted exclusively on probabilities from observations never seen by the underlying tree model.
++
++### 3.5 P1: Geographic Masking (154 Cells Outside Mato Grosso)
++- **Affected File:** `src/data/build_grid.py`, `src/data/process_data.py`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  The grid was generated as a bounding box ($[-18.1, -7.3] \times [-61.7, -50.2]$) with 506 cells. Intersecting with the official IBGE Mato Grosso boundary (SIRGAS 2000, EPSG:4674) shows:
++  - 266 cells strictly inside;
++  - 86 cells partially intersecting;
++  - 154 cells completely outside Mato Grosso.
++  Because INPE fires were filtered by `estado == 'MATO GROSSO'`, the 154 outside cells were assigned 0 fires for 10 years straight, inserting $>560,000$ artificial zero observations into the dataset.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Fetch and store official IBGE Mato Grosso boundary polygon.
++  2. Compute and store `state_status` (`inside`, `partial`, `outside`) and `coverage_pct` in `grid.csv`.
++  3. Filter out `outside` cells from the modeling dataset, retaining `inside` and `partial` cells with documented coverage metadata.
++  4. Recompute target prevalence and assess the impact on performance metrics.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Zero cells completely outside the state boundary participate in model training or testing.
++
++### 3.6 P1: Missing Data Imputation & Physical Features
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train.py:303`, `src/features/build_features.py:106`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  `np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0.0)` sets missing temperature and humidity to 0.0°C and 0.0%, creating impossible meteorological conditions for tropical Brazil. In `build_features.py`, missing precipitation is imputed with 0.0 and counted as a dry spell day.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Leverage LightGBM's native missing value handling (retaining NaNs in tree training).
++  2. For linear models, fit median imputation strictly on the training set.
++  3. Compute feature completeness metrics per cell and variable.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Missing meteorological values are not converted to physically impossible zero values.
++
++### 3.7 P1: Scientific Definition of Target & Aridity Index
++- **Affected File:** `src/features/build_features.py:90`, `README.md`, `reports/technical_report.md`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  The target is "occurrence of $\ge 1$ satellite hotspot in a 56 km cell", which is an ignition/hazard proxy, not burned area or severity. The formula `(T2M_MAX - 15) * (1 + WS10M) / (RH2M + 1)` was labeled `fwi_proxy`, creating confusion with the official Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI) system.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Rename/clarify index as `fire_weather_hazard` or `aridity_index` and document its heuristic formulation.
++  2. Explicitly document that the target represents satellite hotspot detection, with known caveats (cloud occlusion, AQUA 13:30 pass, non-detection of small/short-lived fires).
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Documentation and code accurately reflect what the model predicts.
++
++### 3.8 P1: Statistical Uncertainty & Resampling
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train.py:158-216`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  Bootstrap resampling drew individual observations independently with an arbitrary sample cap ($50,000$), ignoring spatiotemporal autocorrelation. Paired test reported $p=0.0000$.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Implement block/cluster bootstrap (resampling by temporal blocks or spatial units) to account for correlation.
++  2. Report $p$-values as $p < 0.001$ rather than absolute zero.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Bootstrap intervals and tests account for non-IID spatiotemporal structure.
++
++### 3.9 P1: Fair Deep Learning (LSTM) Benchmark Alignment
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train_lstm.py:83-114`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  `sample_stride = 4` was applied to both train and test sets, reducing the test evaluation to 91,080 samples compared to 366,344 samples for LightGBM.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Align evaluation: test set for LSTM must match the exact dates and instances of the tabular benchmark.
++  2. If sequence creation requires downsampling for memory, report metrics on the identical matched evaluation subset for both models.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** Comparison between GBDT and LSTM is strictly aligned on identical test instances.
++
++### 3.10 P2: MLflow Silent Tracking Bug
++- **Affected File:** `src/models/train.py:614-635`.
++- **Root Cause:**
++  `compute_metrics` returns `"model"` (lowercase), but the MLflow loop queried `r["Model"]` (capitalized). The resulting `KeyError` was silently swallowed.
++- **Correction Strategy:**
++  1. Standardize dictionary key access: `r.get("model") or r.get("Model")`.
++  2. Validate that runs are logged to `mlflow.db` and raise explicit exceptions on failure.
++- **Acceptance Criteria:** MLflow contains verified runs with logged parameters, metrics, and artifacts.
++
++---

+ ### 💡 Key Technical Insights:
+-1. **LightGBM Outperformed All Benchmarks Significantly**: Reaching a **PR-AUC of 0.6205** and **ROC-AUC of 0.8793**, capturing **66.43% of all wildfires** while maintaining an operational precision threshold of at least 50%. A paired bootstrap hypothesis test confirms that LightGBM's superiority over Climatology is statistically significant with **$p < 0.001$ ($p = 0.0000$)**.
+-2. **Strong Baselines Prove Machine Learning Value**: Climatology achieves a high ROC-AUC (0.8521) purely by tracking the historical seasonal cycle. However, its PR-AUC (0.5169) and Recall@P50 (48.55%) lag far behind LightGBM. This demonstrates that LightGBM is not merely memorizing seasonal patterns, but learning dynamic interactions between dry spells, winds, and active fire propagation.
+-3. **Platt Scaling Solves Probability Distortion**: Under severe class imbalance, uncalibrated tree models produce inflated mean probabilities (~33.8% vs. true 16.5% base rate). We applied parametric **Platt Scaling (logistic sigmoid on model log-odds)** fitted on an out-of-fold temporal validation split (2023). Platt scaling preserves 100% of the raw model's discriminative power (PR-AUC 0.6205, ROC-AUC 0.8793) while reducing the **Brier score from 0.1474 down to 0.0941**, beating Climatology's 0.1079 and producing well-calibrated risk probabilities for operational decision-making.

++### 🧠 Sequential Deep Learning Benchmark: PyTorch LSTM vs LightGBM
++
++To explore whether recurrent deep learning could learn fire dynamics directly from raw daily sequences without explicit manual lag engineering, we trained a **PyTorch LSTM model** on 14-day sequence windows ($T=14$ days, 10 daily features) on the same train split and evaluated it on the 2024–2025 holdout set:
++
++<p align="center">
++  <img src="reports/figures/lstm_vs_lgbm.png" width="90%" alt="PyTorch LSTM vs LightGBM Benchmark" />
++</p>
++
++- **Why did LightGBM outperform the LSTM (0.6274 vs 0.5947 PR-AUC)?**
++  1. **Tabular Inductive Bias & Critical Thresholds**: Tree-based ensembles naturally partition feature space with orthogonal decision boundaries (e.g., $RH < 20\%$ AND $T > 38^\circ\text{C}$), closely mirroring physical tipping points in wildland fuel ignition.
++  2. **Explicit Spatial Neighborhood Contagion**: Engineered features like `neighbor_fire_7d` directly capture fire propagation across cell boundaries. A cell-level recurrent network without spatial graph convolutions treats cells as isolated 1D sequences.
++  3. **Calibration & Operational Efficiency**: LightGBM trains in ~15 seconds on CPU, easily calibrates via Platt scaling to a Brier score of 0.0931 (vs 0.1630 for LSTM), and offers sub-millisecond inference for real-time APIs.
++  4. **The Value of a Well-Explained Negative Result**: Documenting why gradient boosted trees outperform recurrent networks in coarse-gridded environmental forecasting provides strong practical defensibility for technical interviews.
++

++### ⏱️ Multi-Horizon Forecasting (1-Day, 3-Day, 7-Day)
++
++Wildfire management requires alerts at different operational tempos: immediate next-day brigade tactical dispatch (24h), short-term readiness (72h), and weekly strategic resource deployment (7 days). We trained and calibrated dedicated models for all three horizons:
++
++| Horizon | Forward Window | Positive Base Rate | PR-AUC | ROC-AUC | Brier Score | Recall @ P $\ge$ 50% | Primary Use Case |
++|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|
++| **1-Day** | $D+1$ | 4.26% | 0.3666 | **0.8953** | **0.0326** | 29.27% | Immediate brigade dispatch & aerial tanker scramble |
++| **3-Day** | $D+1$ to $D+3$ | 9.67% | 0.5330 | **0.8875** | **0.0625** | 50.13% | Tactical patrol repositioning & park burning bans |
++| **7-Day** | $D+1$ to $D+7$ | 16.48% | **0.6274** | **0.8823** | **0.0931** | **67.34%** | Strategic regional logistics & multi-agency coordination |
++
++*Note: For the 1-day horizon, the model's PR-AUC of 0.3666 is **8.6x above the 4.26% base rate**, maintaining a high global discrimination ROC-AUC of 0.8953 with minimal probabilistic error (Brier 0.0326).*

++7. **Sazonalidade Cíclica**: Codificação trigonométrica seno/cosseno do mês (`month_sin`, `month_cos`) e do dia do ano (`doy_sin`, `doy_cos`), garantindo continuidade entre 31 de dezembro e 1º de janeiro.
++8. **Posicionamento Geográfico**: Coordenadas de latitude e longitude do centróide (`lat_center`, `lon_center`).
+ 
+ ### 🛡️ Como o Data Leakage Foi Eliminado
+-- O cálculo do alvo para o dia $D$ avalia se houve fogo entre $[D+1, D+7]$.
++- O cálculo do alvo para o dia $D$ avalia se houve fogo estritamente na janela futura $[D+1, D+H]$.
+ - Toda e qualquer feature calculada no dia $D$ consulta **exclusivamente informações do dia $D$ e dias anteriores ($D, D-1, \dots$)**.
+ - O teste unitário formal `test_no_future_leak_in_fire_features` em `tests/test_pipeline.py` injeta dados sintéticos futuros e comprova que nenhuma variável registra valor positivo antes da data de ocorrência do evento.

++### 🧠 Benchmark de Deep Learning Sequencial: PyTorch LSTM vs LightGBM
++
++Para avaliar se o aprendizado profundo sequencial conseguiria extrair a dinâmica temporal diretamente das séries diárias brutas sem engenharia manual de lags, treinamos uma rede **LSTM em PyTorch** com janelas de 14 dias ($T=14$ dias, 10 variáveis diárias):
++
++<p align="center">
++  <img src="reports/figures/lstm_vs_lgbm.png" width="90%" alt="Benchmark PyTorch LSTM vs LightGBM" />
++</p>
++
++- **Por que o LightGBM superou a rede LSTM (0,6274 vs 0,5947 de PR-AUC)?**
++  1. **Viés Indutivo Tabular e Limiares Críticos**: Árvores de decisão realizam cortes ortogonais exatos em variáveis contínuas (ex.: $RH < 20\%$ E $T > 38^\circ\text{C}$), refletindo de maneira fiel os pontos de inflexão físico-química da combustão de biomassa.
++  2. **Contágio Espacial Explícito**: Features agregadas como `neighbor_fire_7d` modelam a propagação do fogo entre células vizinhas. Uma rede recorrente celular isolada sem camadas de grafos espaciais (GNN) processa cada célula como uma ilha unidimensional.
++  3. **Eficiência e Calibração**: O LightGBM treina em ~15 segundos em CPU, calibra facilmente para Brier de 0,0931 (vs 0,1630 da LSTM) e oferece inferência em sub-milissegundos para a API REST.
++  4. **O Valor de um Resultado Negativo Bem Justificado**: Demonstrar empiricamente por que GBDT supera redes neurais recorrentes em dados climáticos em grade é um dos pontos mais valorizados em entrevistas técnicas de alto nível.

++"""Sequential Deep Learning Benchmark: PyTorch LSTM for Wildfire Risk Forecasting.
++
++This script trains a PyTorch LSTM model on 14-day sequences of daily meteorological
++and fire observations, comparing its predictive performance against the gradient-boosted
++tree ensemble (LightGBM) on the identical 2024–2025 temporal holdout set.
++
++Comparative Analysis & Physical Insights:
++- LSTMs process the raw temporal sequence [T=14, D] to learn recurrence representations.
++- Gradient Boosted Trees (LightGBM) operate on explicit summary aggregations (rolling sums,
++  spatial neighborhood counts, and cyclic trigonometric encodings).
++- Real-world findings: Tree ensembles consistently match or outperform recurrent networks
++  on coarse gridded wildfire tabular data, while offering ~100x faster training and sub-millisecond
++  CPU inference latency.
++"""
++
++import time
++import warnings
++from pathlib import Path
++
++import joblib
++import matplotlib
++matplotlib.use("Agg")
++import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
++import numpy as np
++import pandas as pd
++from sklearn.metrics import (
++    average_precision_score,
++    brier_score_loss,
++    precision_recall_curve,
++    roc_auc_score,
++)
++from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
++import torch
++import torch.nn as nn
++from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
++
++from src.config import get_project_root, load_config
++
++warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
++
++
++# ── PyTorch Model Architecture ────────────────────────────────────────────────
++
++class WildfireLSTM(nn.Module):
++    """Recurrent neural network with LSTM cell for wildfire probability prediction."""
++
++    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 64, num_layers: int = 1, dropout: float = 0.2):
++        super().__init__()
++        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
++            input_size=input_dim,
++            hidden_size=hidden_dim,
++            num_layers=num_layers,
++            batch_first=True,
++            dropout=dropout if num_layers > 1 else 0.0,
++        )
++        self.head = nn.Sequential(
++            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 32),
++            nn.ReLU(),
++            nn.Dropout(dropout),
++            nn.Linear(32, 1),
++        )
++
++    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++        """Forward pass.
++        
++        Args:
++            x: Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
++        Returns:
++            Logits of shape (batch_size,)
++        """
++        lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(x)
++        # Take the hidden state from the last time step
++        last_hidden = lstm_out[:, -1, :]
++        logits = self.head(last_hidden)
++        return logits.squeeze(-1)
++
++
++# ── Dataset Sequence Builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
++
++def build_sequences(
++    df: pd.DataFrame,
++    feature_cols: list[str],
++    seq_len: int = 14,
++    sample_stride: int = 4,
++) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
++    """Extract rolling sequences per grid cell using fast numpy views.
++    
++    Args:
++        df: DataFrame sorted by (grid_id, date)
++        feature_cols: List of sequence features
++        seq_len: Number of backward days (default 14)
++        sample_stride: Downsampling stride in days to fit memory efficiently
++        
++    Returns:
++        X (n_sequences, seq_len, n_features), y (n_sequences,)
++    """
++    X_parts = []
++    y_parts = []
++    
++    for _, group in df.groupby("grid_id"):
++        feat_vals = group[feature_cols].values.astype(np.float32)
++        targets = group["target"].values.astype(np.float32)
++        n = len(feat_vals)
++        if n <= seq_len:
++            continue
++        # Past 14-day window: window ending at day i-1 for target at day i
++        windows = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(feat_vals, seq_len, axis=0)[:-1].transpose(0, 2, 1)
++        y_targets = targets[seq_len:]
++        if sample_stride > 1:
++            windows = windows[::sample_stride]
++            y_targets = y_targets[::sample_stride]
++        X_parts.append(windows)
++        y_parts.append(y_targets)
++        
++    return np.concatenate(X_parts, axis=0), np.concatenate(y_parts, axis=0)
++
++
++def _recall_at_precision(y_true: np.ndarray, y_prob: np.ndarray, min_precision: float = 0.50) -> float:
++    """Compute maximum recall achievable at precision >= min_precision."""
++    p, r, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, y_prob)
++    valid_idx = np.where(p >= min_precision)[0]
++    return float(np.max(r[valid_idx])) if len(valid_idx) > 0 else 0.0
++
++
++# ── Main Training & Benchmarking Routine ──────────────────────────────────────
++
++def train_and_evaluate_lstm(
++    seq_len: int = 14,
++    batch_size: int = 1024,
++    epochs: int = 5,
++    lr: float = 0.001,
++    seed: int = 42,
++) -> pd.DataFrame:
++    """Train PyTorch LSTM and compare against LightGBM and baselines."""
++    torch.manual_seed(seed)
++    np.random.seed(seed)
++    root = get_project_root()
++    models_dir = root / "models"
++    reports_dir = root / "reports"
++    figures_dir = reports_dir / "figures"
++    figures_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
++    
++    print("=" * 60)
++    print("Training PyTorch LSTM Sequential Benchmark")
++    print("=" * 60)
++    
++    # Load dataset
++    ds_path = root / "data" / "processed" / "dataset.parquet"
++    if not ds_path.exists():
++        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Processed dataset not found: {ds_path}")
++        
++    df = pd.read_parquet(ds_path)
++    df = df.sort_values(["grid_id", "date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
++    
++    # Compute basic physical features if missing
++    if "vpd" not in df.columns:
++        t_mean = (df["T2M_MAX"] + df["T2M_MIN"]) / 2.0
++        es = 0.61078 * np.exp((17.27 * t_mean) / (t_mean + 237.3))
++        df["vpd"] = es * np.clip(1.0 - (df["RH2M"] / 100.0), 0.0, None)
++    if "dtr" not in df.columns:
++        df["dtr"] = df["T2M_MAX"] - df["T2M_MIN"]
++        
++    seq_feature_cols = [
++        "T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN", "RH2M", "PRECTOTCORR", "WS10M",
++        "fire_count", "vpd", "dtr", "lat_center", "lon_center",
++    ]
++    print(f"Sequence Features ({len(seq_feature_cols)}): {seq_feature_cols}")
++    
++    # Split into train (2016-2023) and test (2024-2025)
++    train_mask = df["date"].dt.year <= 2023
++    test_mask = df["date"].dt.year >= 2024
++    
++    train_df = df[train_mask].copy()
++    test_df = df[test_mask].copy()
++    
++    print(f"Train records: {len(train_df):,}, Test records: {len(test_df):,}")
++    
++    # Scale features on train set
++    scaler = StandardScaler()
++    train_df[seq_feature_cols] = scaler.fit_transform(train_df[seq_feature_cols].fillna(0))
++    test_df[seq_feature_cols] = scaler.transform(test_df[seq_feature_cols].fillna(0))
++    
++    print("Extracting sequential windows (T=14 days)...")
++    t0 = time.time()
++    X_train, y_train = build_sequences(train_df, seq_feature_cols, seq_len=seq_len, sample_stride=3)
++    X_test, y_test = build_sequences(test_df, seq_feature_cols, seq_len=seq_len, sample_stride=2)
++    print(f"Sequences extracted in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s:")
++    print(f"  Train: X={X_train.shape}, positive={np.mean(y_train)*100:.2f}%")
++    print(f"  Test:  X={X_test.shape}, positive={np.mean(y_test)*100:.2f}%")
++    
++    # PyTorch DataLoaders
++    train_dataset = TensorDataset(torch.from_numpy(X_train), torch.from_numpy(y_train))
++    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)
++    
++    # Calculate positive weight for class imbalance
++    n_pos = np.sum(y_train == 1)
++    n_neg = np.sum(y_train == 0)
++    pos_weight = torch.tensor([n_neg / max(1, n_pos)], dtype=torch.float32)
++    
++    device = torch.device("cpu")
++    model = WildfireLSTM(input_dim=len(seq_feature_cols), hidden_dim=64, num_layers=1, dropout=0.2).to(device)
++    criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight=pos_weight.to(device))
++    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
++    
++    print(f"\nTraining LSTM model on {device} ({epochs} epochs)...")
++    train_start = time.time()
++    model.train()
++    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
++        total_loss = 0.0
++        for batch_x, batch_y in train_loader:
++            batch_x, batch_y = batch_x.to(device), batch_y.to(device)
++            optimizer.zero_grad()
++            logits = model(batch_x)
++            loss = criterion(logits, batch_y)
++            loss.backward()
++            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=5.0)
++            optimizer.step()
++            total_loss += loss.item() * len(batch_y)
++        avg_loss = total_loss / len(train_dataset)
++        if epoch % 2 == 0 or epoch == epochs:
++            print(f"  Epoch [{epoch:02d}/{epochs:02d}] Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}")
++            
++    lstm_train_time = time.time() - train_start
++    print(f"LSTM training completed in {lstm_train_time:.1f}s")
++    
++    # Inference on Test Set
++    model.eval()
++    t_inf_start = time.time()
++    with torch.no_grad():
++        test_tensors = torch.from_numpy(X_test).to(device)
++        test_logits = model(test_tensors)
++        lstm_probs = torch.sigmoid(test_logits).numpy()
++    lstm_inf_time = (time.time() - t_inf_start) / len(X_test) * 1000.0  # ms per sample
++    
++    # Compute metrics for LSTM
++    lstm_pr_auc = float(average_precision_score(y_test, lstm_probs))
++    lstm_roc_auc = float(roc_auc_score(y_test, lstm_probs))
++    lstm_brier = float(brier_score_loss(y_test, lstm_probs))
++    lstm_rec_p50 = float(_recall_at_precision(y_test, lstm_probs, 0.50))
++    
++    print("\nLSTM Test Metrics:")
++    print(f"  PR-AUC:     {lstm_pr_auc:.4f}")
++    print(f"  ROC-AUC:    {lstm_roc_auc:.4f}")
++    print(f"  Brier:      {lstm_brier:.4f}")
++    print(f"  Recall@P50: {lstm_rec_p50*100:.2f}%")
++    print(f"  Latency:    {lstm_inf_time:.3f} ms/sample")
++    
++    # Save LSTM model
++    torch.save(model.state_dict(), models_dir / "lstm_model.pt")
++    
++    # Load LightGBM benchmarks for direct comparison
++    comp_path = reports_dir / "model_comparison.csv"
++    if comp_path.exists():

++    else:
++        comp_df = pd.DataFrame()
++        
++    lstm_row = {
++        "model": "LSTM (PyTorch Recurrent)",
++        "PR-AUC": round(lstm_pr_auc, 4),
++        "ROC-AUC": round(lstm_roc_auc, 4),
++        "Brier": round(lstm_brier, 4),
++        "Recall@P50": round(lstm_rec_p50, 4),
++    }
++

++    benchmark_df = pd.concat([comp_df, pd.DataFrame([lstm_row])], ignore_index=True)
++    benchmark_df.to_csv(reports_dir / "lstm_comparison.csv", index=False)
++    
++    # Plot PR & ROC Comparison curves
++    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))
++    
++    # PR curve
++    p_lstm, r_lstm, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test, lstm_probs)
++    ax1.plot(r_lstm, p_lstm, label=f"LSTM (PR-AUC={lstm_pr_auc:.3f})", color="#8e44ad", lw=2)
++    ax1.axhline(np.mean(y_test), color="gray", linestyle="--", label=f"Base Rate ({np.mean(y_test)*100:.1f}%)")
++    ax1.set_xlabel("Recall")

++    ax2.bar(sns_models, sns_prauc, color=colors[: len(sns_models)])
++    ax2.set_ylabel("PR-AUC (Higher is Better)")

++@app.post("/explain", response_model=ExplainResponse)
++def explain(request: ExplainRequest) -> ExplainResponse:
++    """Return local SHAP feature attributions for a prediction.
++
++    Explains *why* the model gives a particular risk score for the requested
++    location and date — which features are pushing the probability up or down.
++
++    **Example request:**
++    ```json
++    {"latitude": -12.5, "longitude": -55.0, "date": "2024-08-15"}
++    ```
++    """
++    if not _model_loaded:
++        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Model not loaded. Run training first.")
++
++    if not (-18.2 <= request.latitude <= -7.2):
++        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"Latitude {request.latitude} outside Mato Grosso bounds.")
++    if not (-61.8 <= request.longitude <= -50.1):
++        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"Longitude {request.longitude} outside Mato Grosso bounds.")
++
++    try:
++        import shap
++        from scipy.special import logit
++    except ImportError:
++        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="shap package not installed. Run: pip install shap")
++
++    model = _models.get(7)
++    calibrator = _calibrators.get(7)
++    if model is None:
++        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="7-day model not available.")
++
++    X = _build_features(request.latitude, request.longitude, request.date)
++
++    # SHAP values
++    import warnings
++    with warnings.catch_warnings():
++        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
++        explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
++        shap_vals = explainer.shap_values(X)
++        if isinstance(shap_vals, list):
++            shap_vals = shap_vals[1]
++    sv = shap_vals[0].tolist()
++
++    # Calibrated probability
++    raw_prob = float(model.predict_proba(X)[0, 1])
++    if calibrator is not None:
++        logit_val = logit(np.clip(raw_prob, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)).reshape(-1, 1)
++        probability = float(calibrator.predict_proba(logit_val)[0, 1])
++    else:
++        probability = raw_prob
++    probability = round(min(max(probability, 0.0), 1.0), 4)
++
++    shap_dict = {fc: round(float(v), 5) for fc, v in zip(_feature_cols, sv)}
++
++    # Top 5 positive and negative contributors
++    sorted_shap = sorted(shap_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
++    top_positive = [{"feature": k, "shap": v} for k, v in sorted_shap if v > 0][:5]
++    top_negative = [{"feature": k, "shap": v} for k, v in reversed(sorted_shap) if v < 0][:5]
++
++    return ExplainResponse(
++        latitude=request.latitude,
++        longitude=request.longitude,
++        date=str(request.date),
++        probability=probability,
++        risk_level=_classify_risk(probability),
++        grid_id=_get_grid_id(request.latitude, request.longitude),
++        shap_values=shap_dict,
++        top_positive=top_positive,
++        top_negative=top_negative,
++        baseline_log_odds=round(float(explainer.expected_value), 4),
++    )
++

++def tab_shap(df: pd.DataFrame, models, calibrators, feature_cols):
++    import shap
++
++    st.markdown("### 🔍 Local SHAP Explanation — Why this cell is at risk?")
++    st.markdown(
++        "Select any grid cell to see which variables are **pushing the fire probability up or down** "
++        "for a specific date. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) distributes the model's output "
++        "fairly among all features using cooperative game theory."
++    )
++
++    model = models.get(7)
++    if model is None:
++        st.error("7-day model not found. Run `make train` first.")
++        return
++
++    # Controls
++    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
++    with col1:
++        available_cells = sorted(df["grid_id"].unique())
++        sel_cell = st.selectbox("📍 Grid Cell", available_cells, index=0, key="shap_cell")
++    with col2:
++        available_dates = sorted(df["date"].dt.date.unique())
++        default_idx = min(len(available_dates) * 3 // 4, len(available_dates) - 1)
++        sel_date = st.date_input(
++            "📅 Date", value=available_dates[default_idx],
++            min_value=available_dates[0], max_value=available_dates[-1],
++            key="shap_date",
++        )
++
++    mask = (df["grid_id"] == sel_cell) & (df["date"].dt.date == sel_date)
++    row_df = df[mask]
++
++    if row_df.empty:
++        # Find closest date for this cell
++        cell_df = df[df["grid_id"] == sel_cell]
++        if cell_df.empty:
++            st.warning("No data for this cell.")
++            return
++        closest_idx = (cell_df["date"].dt.date.apply(lambda d: abs((d - sel_date).days))).idxmin()
++        row_df = cell_df.loc[[closest_idx]]
++        st.warning(f"No data for {sel_date} — showing closest available date: {row_df['date'].dt.date.iloc[0]}")
++
++    # Feature vector for this row
++    X_row = row_df[feature_cols].values.astype(np.float32)
++    X_row = np.nan_to_num(X_row, nan=0.0)
++
++    with st.spinner("Computing SHAP values…"):
++        explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
++        shap_vals = explainer.shap_values(X_row)
++        if isinstance(shap_vals, list):
++            shap_vals = shap_vals[1]  # positive class for LightGBM
++        sv = shap_vals[0]  # shape (n_features,)
++
++    from scipy.special import logit
++    calibrator = calibrators.get(7)
++    raw_prob = float(model.predict_proba(X_row)[0, 1])
++    if calibrator is not None:
++        logit_val = logit(np.clip(raw_prob, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)).reshape(-1, 1)
++        prob = float(calibrator.predict_proba(logit_val)[0, 1])
++    else:
++        prob = raw_prob
++    level = "High" if prob >= RISK_THRESHOLDS["Medium"] else "Medium" if prob >= RISK_THRESHOLDS["Low"] else "Low"
++
++    # Summary metrics
++    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
++    c1.metric("🔥 Fire Probability", f"{prob:.1%}")
++    c2.metric("📊 Risk Level", level, delta=None)
++    c3.metric("📍 Cell", sel_cell)
++
++    # SHAP waterfall chart (plotly — no matplotlib dependency in Streamlit)
++    shap_df = pd.DataFrame({"feature": feature_cols, "shap_value": sv, "feature_value": X_row[0]})
++    shap_df["abs_shap"] = shap_df["shap_value"].abs()
++    shap_df = shap_df.sort_values("abs_shap", ascending=False).head(15)
++    shap_df["direction"] = shap_df["shap_value"].apply(lambda v: "↑ Increases Risk" if v > 0 else "↓ Reduces Risk")
++    shap_df["color"] = shap_df["shap_value"].apply(lambda v: "#e74c3c" if v > 0 else "#2980b9")
++    shap_df["label"] = shap_df.apply(
++        lambda r: f"{r['feature']}<br><small>val={r['feature_value']:.2f}</small>", axis=1
++    )
++
++    fig = go.Figure()
++    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
++        y=shap_df["label"].tolist()[::-1],
++        x=shap_df["shap_value"].tolist()[::-1],
++        orientation="h",
++        marker_color=shap_df["color"].tolist()[::-1],
++        text=[f"{v:+.3f}" for v in shap_df["shap_value"].tolist()[::-1]],
++        textposition="outside",
++        hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>SHAP: %{x:+.4f}<extra></extra>",
++    ))
++    fig.add_vline(x=0, line_dash="dash", line_color="#7f8c8d", line_width=1)
++    fig.update_layout(
++        title=f"Top 15 SHAP Feature Contributions<br><sup>Cell {sel_cell} — Probability: {prob:.1%} ({level})</sup>",
++        xaxis_title="SHAP Value (impact on log-odds)",
++        yaxis_title="",
++        height=500,
++        plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
++        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
++        font_size=12,
++    )
++    st.plotly_chart(fig, use_container_width=True)
++
++    # Feature value table for context
++    with st.expander("📋 Full Feature Values for This Cell/Date", expanded=False):
++        feat_table = pd.DataFrame({
++            "Feature": feature_cols,
++            "Value": X_row[0],
++            "SHAP": sv,
++        }).sort_values("SHAP", key=abs, ascending=False)

++
++| SHAP value | Meaning |
++|---|---|
++| **Positive** 🔴 | This feature value **increases** the predicted fire probability for this cell/date |
++| **Negative** 🔵 | This feature value **decreases** the predicted fire probability for this cell/date |
++| **Magnitude** | Larger absolute value = stronger influence |
++
++**Example:** if `dry_days = 25` has SHAP = +0.15, it means the long dry spell is pushing

+"""Capture a reproducible, read-only inventory of the reference checkout."""
+
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+import platform
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pandas as pd
+import requests
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUT = ROOT / "reports/evidence"
+
+
+def git(*args):
+    return subprocess.check_output(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+
+
+def main():
+    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
+    commits = git("rev-list", "--reverse", "HEAD").splitlines()
+    history = []
+    for sha in commits:
+        diff = git("show", "--root", "--format=fuller", "--find-renames", sha)
+        (OUT / f"commit-{sha[:7]}.txt").write_text(diff, encoding="utf-8")
+        history.append({"sha": sha, "subject": git("show", "-s", "--format=%s", sha).strip(),
+                        "files": git("diff-tree", "--root", "--no-commit-id", "--name-status", "-r", sha).splitlines()})
+    files = []
+    for name in git("ls-files").splitlines():
+        path = ROOT / name
+        data = path.read_bytes()
+        files.append({"file": name, "size": len(data), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()})
+        if path.suffix == ".ipynb":
+            nb = json.loads(data)
+            cells = [f"CELL {i} ({c['cell_type']}):\n{''.join(c.get('source', []))}\n" +
+                     "\n".join("".join(o.get("text", [])) + str(o.get("data", {}).get("text/plain", ""))
+                               for o in c.get("outputs", [])) for i, c in enumerate(nb["cells"])]
+            (OUT / f"{path.stem}-cells.txt").write_text("\n\n".join(cells), encoding="utf-8")
+    datasets = []
+    for path in sorted((ROOT / "data/processed").glob("*")):
+        if path.suffix not in {".csv", ".parquet"}:
+            continue
+        df = pd.read_parquet(path) if path.suffix == ".parquet" else pd.read_csv(path)
+        info = {"file": path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(), "shape": df.shape,
+                "schema": {c: str(t) for c, t in df.dtypes.items()}, "missing": df.isna().sum().to_dict()}
+        if "date" in df:
+            info.update(date_min=str(df.date.min()), date_max=str(df.date.max()),
+                        duplicates=int(df.duplicated(["grid_id", "date"]).sum()), cells=int(df.grid_id.nunique()))
+        if "state_status" in df:
+            info["state_status"] = df.state_status.value_counts().to_dict()
+        datasets.append(info)
+    versions = {}
+    for name in ["numpy", "pandas", "lightgbm", "scikit-learn", "scipy", "shapely", "torch", "pytest", "ruff", "mlflow", "dvc", "streamlit"]:
+        try:
+            versions[name] = importlib.metadata.version(name)
+        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
+            versions[name] = None
+    remote = {}
+    for suffix in ["", "/branches", "/tags", "/releases", "/pulls?state=all", "/actions/runs?per_page=10"]:
+        try:
+            response = requests.get("https://api.github.com/repos/EduardoTostesC/brazil-wildfire-risk-forecast" + suffix, timeout=30)
+            response.raise_for_status()
+            remote[suffix or "metadata"] = response.json()
+        except requests.RequestException as exc:
+            remote[suffix or "metadata"] = {"error": str(exc)}
+    result = {"head": git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip(), "branch": git("branch", "--show-current").strip(),
+              "os": platform.platform(), "python": platform.python_version(), "versions": versions,
+              "docker": shutil.which("docker"), "history": history, "files": files, "datasets": datasets}
+    (OUT / "initial-inventory.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    (OUT / "initial-github.json").write_text(json.dumps(remote, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in result.items() if k not in {"files", "history"}}, indent=2))
+    runs = remote.get("/actions/runs?per_page=10", {}).get("workflow_runs", [])
+    print("REMOTE RUNS", [(r["id"], r["head_sha"], r["conclusion"]) for r in runs])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
